---
title: Versions and citation
description: latest vs dated releases on R2 and the permanent tags on Hugging Face, how to pin a version, and how to cite Cancer Basemap.
---

Cancer Basemap publishes one kind of release, a folder of Parquet files plus a
DuckDB database, in two places. They hold the same tables in the same layout.
They differ in how long they last and how you use them
([ADR-0001](https://github.com/seandavi/cancer-basemap/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-public-releases-monthly-parquet-bundles.md)).
[Releases](../releases.qmd) lists the ones available now.

| Version | Where | Changes? | Kept | Use it by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `latest/` | `https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/` | with each release | always the newest | querying in place |
| Dated | `https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/v{YYYY-MM-DD}/` | never | the newest release of each of the 12 newest months that had one | querying in place |
| Tag | Hugging Face dataset `seandavis/cancerbasemap`, git tag `YYYY-MM-DD` | never | permanently, every release | downloading, then querying locally |

A release is cut on the 1st of each month, and by hand when a correction or a
large new source release can't wait. `latest/` and the dated folders on R2 are
served for querying in place: DuckDB `ATTACH`, `read_parquet` and the
[playground](../playground.qmd) all read them over HTTPS. Every release is
also pushed to Hugging Face and tagged with its date, and tags are never
deleted. A tag is the version to cite. Download one, then query it locally.

::: callout-note
R2 keeps the newest release of each of the 12 newest months that had a
release. A release that a same-month correction replaced is deleted 7 days
after the correction. So a dated folder is a short-to-medium-term pin, not an
archive; anything older, or replaced, is on Hugging Face only, where the
release keeps its tag.
:::

## Which one to use

- Exploring, or building something that should track the sources: use `latest/`.
- An analysis you'll rerun soon: pin a dated folder.
- A paper, a report, a shared pipeline, or anything that must stay reproducible or that you'll cite: download the Hugging Face tag `YYYY-MM-DD`.

## Pin a dated folder

Replace `latest/` with a date. Each dated folder's `cancerbasemap.duckdb` reads
its own Parquet files, so the views stay pinned too:

```{.sql .no-shell}
ATTACH 'https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/v2026-12-01/cancerbasemap.duckdb' AS basemap (READ_ONLY);
```

To see which dates are available, open [Releases](../releases.qmd) or the
[folder listing](https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/). A dated folder can
disappear: when its month ages out of the 12 newest, or 7 days after a
same-month correction replaces it. Use a tag for anything that must stay
reproducible.

## Use a tag

Every release that passes the gate is copied to the Hugging Face dataset
`seandavis/cancerbasemap` and tagged with its date (the R2 folder
`v2026-12-01/` is the tag `2026-12-01`). Files sit at the repository root in
the same layout as R2 (`measure/observation.parquet`, …).

Download the release with the [`hf` command-line
tool](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/guides/cli) (in
`huggingface_hub`; `uvx --from huggingface_hub hf` runs it without
installing), then query the local files:

```bash
hf download seandavis/cancerbasemap --repo-type dataset --revision 2026-12-01 \
  --local-dir cancerbasemap-2026-12-01
duckdb -c "SELECT count(*) FROM 'cancerbasemap-2026-12-01/measure/observation.parquet'"
```

`--include 'measure/*'` downloads only some of the files. A [Hugging Face
token](https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens) (`hf auth login`) raises the
download rate limits.

Don't query the archive in place with `hf://` paths. Hugging Face limits
anonymous requests, one query can make hundreds, and repeated queries soon fail
with HTTP 429. For in-place queries use `latest/` or a dated folder.

## Cite Cancer Basemap

Cite the release you used by its tag (e.g. `seandavis/cancerbasemap@2026-12-01`),
and its DOI if the dataset page for that tag shows one. A tag is permanent
even after its R2 folder is deleted.

If you used a dated folder, its date is the tag. Also record the `release` and
`git_sha` from its `manifest.json`. Each table also names the upstream source
and release it came from, and each source keeps its own terms; cite those
sources as they ask (see [Sources](../sources.qmd)).

## The manifest

Every version has a `manifest.json`:

```bash
curl -s https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/manifest.json
```

DuckDB reads it directly. The provenance fields of the current `latest/`:

```sql
SELECT release, published_at, git_sha
FROM read_json('https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/manifest.json');
```

And the row count of each published table:

```sql
SELECT t.schema, t."table", t.row_count
FROM read_json('https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/manifest.json'),
     unnest(tables) AS u(t)
ORDER BY t.schema, t."table";
```

- `release` is the release date and `git_sha` the commit of the [pipeline code](https://github.com/seandavi/cancer-basemap) that built it.
- `provenance` lists each upstream release the data was built from.
- `tables` gives each table's `path`, `row_count`, `bytes`, `sha256`, comment and column docs.
